what: The New York Times sells digital subscriptions to its journalism, plus bundled access to Games, Cooking, The Athletic and Wirecutter, and it still prints a newspaper.
customers: About 12 million subscribers, mostly digital, plus advertisers and licensing partners.
money: licensing, Wirecutter affiliate revenue and events
moat: A newsroom of a scale almost nobody else funds, and a bundle where Games and Cooking keep people subscribing between big news events.
risks: 28 times earnings for a business growing revenue in the high single digits
Print revenue declines every year and still carries fixed costs
AI answer engines may reduce the search traffic that brings new readers
opportunities: A 12.2% net margin and $593M of free cash flow, with $642M of cash against $49M of debt
Revenue grew from $2.1B to $2.8B in four years, almost all from digital subscriptions
Bundle subscribers pay more and cancel less than news-only subscribers, and the bundle keeps growing
watch: Net digital subscriber additions and average revenue per subscriber.
